# link-image-reference-definitions

- ID: `MD053`
- Category: Links and images
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `images`, `links`

Every reference definition is used and defined once, except \[//\] comments.

## Why

Definitions render nothing, so an unused one is dead text. Only the first of
duplicate definitions takes effect, so the others change nothing. A definition
labeled //, as in \[//\]: \# (note), is a common way to write a comment, so it
is ignored. A GFM footnote definition such as \[^1\]: A note. counts too where
gomdlint can tell that GitHub reads it as one: at the start of a line outside
lists and blockquotes, with a label of letters, digits and hyphens.

## Options

Set them under `rules.link-image-reference-definitions.options`.

- `ignored_definitions` (`string[]`, default `[//]`): Labels of definitions that
  may go unused. The default, //, allows comments written as \[//\]: \# (text).

## Fix

The fix deletes the unused or duplicate definition. gomdlint reports some
definitions without a fix, such as one that other text follows on the next line,
or one whose label starts with ^, which may be a footnote whose text goes on in
later lines. gomdlint may report a finding without a fix when the fix would
change a line with one character in brackets, such as \[x\] or \[1\], or the
lines around it up to a blank line, because it could add or remove a task list
checkbox.

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  link-image-reference-definitions:
    options:
      ignored_definitions: [//]
```

Under `rules`, `link-image-reference-definitions: false` turns the rule off and
`link-image-reference-definitions: error` reports its findings as errors. The
flag `--disable link-image-reference-definitions` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line link-image-reference-definitions -->
```
